f73f513a6a144a200822c09a.title_original: DetectViT: Test-time Backdoor Detection for Vision Transformers via Inter-Head Attention Discrepancy
f73f513a6a144a200822c09a.excerpt: arXiv:2611.23770v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) now underpin the visual encoders of most multimodal models, but this success comes at a cost: relying on third-party pretrained checkpoints leaves these systems open to backdoor attacks. Existing test-time detection methods rely on either the predicted label or intermediate embeddings, limiting their applicability across diverse tasks and incurring substantial computational overhead. In this work, we study how backdoor triggers affect the multi-head attention mechanism of ViTs and identify two distinct anomalous patterns: $\textit{complete attention hijacking}$, causing the attention to exhibit abnormally high inter-head spatial overlap, and $\textit{partial attention hijacking}$, causing an abnormally large variance in the concentration of the attention distribution. Motivated by these findings, we propose $\textbf{DetectViT}$, a test-time backdoor detection method that requires neither training data, model outputs, nor any prior knowledge of the trigger. DetectViT quantifies the two hijacking phenomena via an inter-head consistency score and an inter-head entropy variance score, with thresholds estimated from a small out-of-distribution (OOD) calibration set drawn from an arbitrary source. Across four representative attacks, diverse architectures (DeiT, CLIP, and LLaVA), and downstream tasks (image classification and captioning), DetectViT substantially outperforms all baselines with as few as 64--

8a97b744a858122914ae26d1.title_original: RECLAIM: Robot-Vision-Informed Adversarial Patch Defense via Embodied Attention Feedback
8a97b744a858122914ae26d1.excerpt: arXiv:2611.24494v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language-action policies control embodied agents through a perception-action loop grounded in physical interaction, where adversarial patches can corrupt action predictions and thereby alter subsequent observations. To mitigate these threats, many existing defenses rely on policy adaptation or auxiliary models, but require additional training or inference. We introduce RECLAIM, a training-free, inference-time defense that uses a frozen VLA's own attention response to local visual interventions to guide purification during closed-loop embodied manipulation. Our key insight is that attention changes induced by local edits provide feedback for choosing where and how to purify as the robot interacts with its environment. RECLAIM combines this feedback with robot geometry to refine patch localization and select local treatments, then revalidates them as the agent's embodied actions change the observed scene. We evaluate RECLAIM against patches generated by four adversarial attack methods across multiple manipulation task suites under frozen VLA control. Under adversarial patch attacks, RECLAIM succeeds in at least one rollout on 95% of the evaluated tasks and raises rollout success on LIBERO-Object from 0% without defense to 70.0%. fd631a0eb8a2c8d8641c0fce.title_original: SCR: Detecting Backdoor-Poisoned Samples through Clean-Reference Residuals
fd631a0eb8a2c8d8641c0fce.excerpt: arXiv:2611.24558v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep neural networks are vulnerable to backdoor attacks, in which adversaries manipulate model predictions by injecting poisoned samples into training data. Detecting these samples remains challenging because legitimate semantic variation can obscure poisoning-related signals in learned representations. Consequently, class-level statistics used by existing detectors may flag benign feature deviations while overlooking poisoned samples that blend into the class distribution. In this paper, we propose Semantic Counterfactual Residualization (SCR), which uses a small set of clean reference samples to account for benign variation through sample-specific feature reconstruction. SCR identifies poisoned samples by detecting coherent deviations from these clean baselines, without requiring prior knowledge of the attacks. We evaluate SCR through experiments covering twelve dirty-label and clean-label attacks across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny ImageNet. With a small clean-reference set, SCR achieves attack-averaged true positive rates above 99.5\% and false positive rates below 2\% on each dataset, outperforming eight representative detection baselines in macro-TPR.

3e74f0a0021dbfd605b02ad4.title_original: Stealing Exact Training Data from Other Clients during Federated Learning
3e74f0a0021dbfd605b02ad4.excerpt: arXiv:2611.24689v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Malicious adversaries can employ gradient inversion attacks to reverse-engineer private data using the model updates of a round in Federated Learning. While there have been developments in gradient inversion for text, exact text recovery by a malicious client has so far remained infeasible, as FedAvg entangles the gradient contributions of many clients and obscures the signal of any individual sentence. We introduce a novel attack pipeline that unwinds this entanglement progressively through an iterative loop, in which the gradient contributions of sentences recovered exactly in one round are subtracted from the aggregate, exposing the remaining sentences for recovery in the next iteration. We show, for the first time, exact sentence recovery, with 100% precision, and on aggregates containing up to $4\times$ more tokens than the model's hidden dimension, we recover up to 80.2% of client sentences exactly, a regime where existing attacks recover none exactly.

2ec7f0e5d0c02bb64ee49888.title_original: "I Don't Think It's a Scam": A First Look at Family Intervention Barriers in Elder Abuse Discussions on Reddit and Baidu Tieba
2ec7f0e5d0c02bb64ee49888.excerpt: arXiv:2611.24899v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When older adults trust scammers despite warnings, families face obstacles to intervention. Complainants aged 60 and older reported \$4.9 billion in losses in 2024 to the U.S. Internet Crime Complaint Center. In Reddit posts recording reactions, account locks or credential changes appeared in 8.9\% under resistance or continued involvement, compared with 33.3\% under acceptance. Measures such as phone or network monitoring and financial takeover were reported more often under resistance. eb713f0e39d52ae61e52ea0f.title_original: Static Attribution of Android Residential Proxy Malware Using Graph Kernels
eb713f0e39d52ae61e52ea0f.excerpt: arXiv:2604.27302v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Android residential proxy applications represent a growing class of potentially-unwanted programs (PUPs) that covertly route third-party traffic through end-user devices, enabling ad fraud, credential abuse, and evasion of geolocation controls by sophisticated threat actors. To support explainability, we map classifier decisions to automatically generated Yara rules, achieving per-family accuracies up to 88.45\% after filtering non-discriminative signatures. Finally, we discuss these results in the context of the broader ecosystem. We find that from the expanded dataset, the majority of applications (51.4\%) still available through APKPure still contain embedded proxy SDK code. 5b11d58b76b25affe41e9df4.title_original: Is Randomness Necessary for Adaptive Data Analysis?
5b11d58b76b25affe41e9df4.excerpt: arXiv:2607.07085v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Adaptive Data Analysis (ADA) problem formalizes the challenge of preventing false discovery and overfitting when a dataset is repeatedly reused. Formally, our input is a dataset containing $n$ i.i.d. samples from an unknown distribution $\mathcal{P}$ over a domain $\mathcal{X}$, and our goal is to answer a sequence of $k$ adaptively chosen statistical queries with respect to $\mathcal{P}$. The main question is how many queries we can support (i.e., how large $k$ can be), primarily as a function of the number of samples $n$. This question has been intensively studied and is relatively well-understood for randomized mechanisms: there are computationally efficient mechanisms that support $k \approx n^2$ queries, and no computationally efficient mechanism can answer $k \gg n^2$ queries. In this paper, we address a fundamental question: is randomness necessary for ADA? Despite a decade of work on ADA, this question remains open. A folklore observation dating back to the initial works on ADA is that randomness is {\em not} necessary when the analyst is computationally bounded. Yet, the necessity of randomness against computationally unbounded analysts has remained elusive. Our main contribution resolves this gap in the information-theoretic setting. Perhaps surprisingly, we show that randomness is {\em strictly necessary} to answer a non-trivial number of adaptive queries: when the analyst is unbounded, any deterministic mecha

0750b25c2ec0cd3a81c3349f.title_original: Language Model Security Modules: Turning LLM Interpretability into Runtime Defense
0750b25c2ec0cd3a81c3349f.excerpt: arXiv:2608.25697v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are served behind layered defenses such as alignment and guardrail models, yet jailbreaks still get through. Interpretability research looks inside the model, where methods such as probes and sparse autoencoders expose signals of harmful content during generation. A signal alone, however, is not a defense. To become one, the serving system must tie each signal to the right request, apply the policy as declared, and release output only when the policy allows. Today, defenses built on such signals handle these duties on their own, so every new detector needs its own integration. Yet none of these duties depends on how a signal is computed. We present Language Model Security Modules (LMSM), which adapts the design of Linux Security Modules to LLM serving and carries out these duties once in a shared mediation path. The path hosts pluggable backends that turn model internals into evidence and policies that decide what that evidence allows. Each policy declares the evidence and evaluations it needs, and LMSM provides exactly these for each request and verifies that they took place, so a failure is never mistaken for permission. Protection therefore remains cheap and correct under common serving optimizations. d0e5013e245d342ea70f1fca.title_original: Threshold Choice, Not Sample Size, Bounds Trustless Verification of Nondeterministic Compound AI Workflows
d0e5013e245d342ea70f1fca.excerpt: arXiv:2609.10601v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Compound AI pipelines chain LLM calls, retrievers, and tools and are nondeterministic: sampling, model updates, and volatile tool responses make one input yield different outputs across runs. Such pipelines increasingly run across edge, cloud, and orbital nodes owned by no single party, whose optimizations discard intermediate results before inspection. Verifying reproduction there means tolerating nondeterministic outputs, a node that may not report honestly, and intermittent access to any shared record; existing work addresses at most two at once. We give a protocol covering all three: it commits digests of each stage's inputs, outputs, and context under a policy digest pinning the metric and threshold, anchors them without trusting the executing node, defers under partition, and decides a challenge on the median of $k$ re-executions, with no quorum. Where that procedure breaks is the main result. On a synthetic HotpotQA pipeline a calibrated fixed threshold accepts 44 of 45 honest reproductions and rejects 104 of 105 divergent pairs, yet lets same-input fabrication through in 27 of 29 trials at k=5, more samples being no help since sampling sharpens an estimate without moving it. Holding that metric and this pipeline's re-execution spread fixed, the binding constraint is the threshold rather than the sample size: one derived per execution detects 19 of 29 where the best constant matched to the same zero honest rejections

fda45d52a4e1781ffb40c731.title_original: PoCoFL: A Framework for POlicy-COmpliant Federated Learning
fda45d52a4e1781ffb40c731.excerpt: arXiv:2610.03650v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a privacy-oriented learning paradigm that enables collaborative model training while keeping training data local to clients. However, FL does not guarantee that clients submit policy-compliant contributions or that aggregators process admitted contributions correctly. Update-magnitude bounds alone cannot ensure compliance with learning-specific requirements involving private data, intermediate models, or retained state. These requirements differ across FL settings, motivating a unified framework to specify and verify client and aggregation policies. This work introduces PoCoFL, a policy-compliant federated learning framework that separates three aspects: (i) FL type, (ii) policy semantics, and (iii) cryptographic realisation. We provide a formalisation that captures client and aggregation requirements as policy-dependent relations, defining update admissibility, aggregation correctness, and policy-relative privacy. These relations enable verification of selected properties of intermediate objects, such as local-model loss, continual-learning state, and personalised optimisation conditions, in each round. Clients demonstrate compliance of their contributions using compatible cryptographic mechanisms, while aggregators prove that the recorded set of admitted contributions was processed according to the selected aggregation policy. We demonstrate PoCoFL through four formal instantiations and correspon

725f27be17ba69555e412300.title_original: Adversarial Process Disturbances at a Deployable Alarm Budget: Detector Evaluation on a Simulator and a Real Plant
725f27be17ba69555e412300.excerpt: arXiv:2610.38786v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Industrial anomaly detection is evaluated largely on simulators, and recent work reports large drops, with unstable rankings, on real plant data. We ask whether that extends to the security case. We evaluate eleven detectors across classical, neural, dependency and causal families on a simulated chemical process and a sodium thermal-hydraulic facility: different processes sharing no equipment, but both continuous, at steady state, and perturbed only through temperature, pressure, flow and valve, never composition. Three conditions prior work does not cover: disturbances authored against a threat model rather than native faults; one construction applied to both processes; and detection read at a declared false-alarm budget. The drop persists throughout. The simulator panel looks deployable, neural matching classical; on plant telemetry detection collapses and the neural family trails, a gap that in-sample thresholds likely understate. Which detector wins transfers between the two processes; how often it fires does not. Two results hold on both. Sequential valve manipulation defeats the whole panel: at tier 2 no detector flags more than 0.17 of its perturbed samples, against 0.89 or better for most disturbances. And the plant's collapse is not merely that its disturbances are weaker, though they are by about twelvefold; matched on measured strength, the plant is never the better detected.

4184feab8a8c0ee7e9eddbdc.title_original: CoordX Protocol: Peer to Peer Cryptographically Verified Shared Records
4184feab8a8c0ee7e9eddbdc.excerpt: arXiv:2611.06034v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: People, companies and software agents often must work on shared records even when they do not trust each other. Today they usually give those records to a central server. The server keeps the canonical copy, authenticates users, and decides who has permissions to act on the record. The CoordX Protocol removes the need for that central server. In the CoordX protocol the author of a record holds full permission over it. Permission for any other party to create, read or update the record is assigned by explicit grants and keys. An invitation only starts contact between two parties. It gives no permission. Each record is a causal tree of signed entries, and each entry is immutable. Each entry names the permission that allowed it. Any party can get the proof of that permission and check it without help from anyone. Two honest parties that check the same bytes, with the same keys and local settings, always get the same answer. The content is encrypted, so the relays that may carry it in transit see only sealed bytes. To exclude a party from future content, the other parties move to new keys. The protocol does not choose a winning version, does not put entries in time order, and does not need global agreement. Applications decide what the entries mean above the level of the protocol.

4db37ebaf773af7cea8e4119.title_original: VerifyPrompt: Towards Text-to-Image Models Verification Behind Black-Box APIs
4db37ebaf773af7cea8e4119.excerpt: arXiv:2410.22725v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: With the rise of diverse Text-to-Image (T2I) models such as DALL-E 3, third-party platforms increasingly integrate multiple black-box APIs to deliver cost-effective services. To address this practical concern, we first define the task of T2I model verification, which determines whether a black-box target model matches a black-box oracle reference model. After that, we propose VerifyPrompt, which performs T2I model verification through a specially designed verify prompt. Intuitively, the verify prompt is an adversarial prompt for the target model, without transferability to other models. It makes the target model generate a specific image while making other models produce entirely different images. Our key idea for generating verify prompts is to enforce strong interactions between adversarial perturbations and the target model, thereby overfitting the target and producing model-specific perturbations. 8f41299349a892a9f29bacf6.title_original: SoK: Market Microstructure for Decentralized Prediction Markets (DePMs)
8f41299349a892a9f29bacf6.excerpt: arXiv:2510.15612v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Decentralized prediction markets (DePMs) allow open participation in event-based wagering without fully relying on centralized intermediaries. We review the history of DePMs which date back to 2011 and includes hundreds of proposals. Perhaps surprising, modern DePMs like Polymarket deviate materially from earlier designs like Truthcoin and Augur v1. We use our review to present a modular workflow comprising eight stages: underlying infrastructure, market topic, share structure and pricing, market initialization, trading, market resolution, settlement, and archiving. For each module, we enumerate the design variants, analyzing trade-offs around decentralization, expressiveness, and manipulation resistance. We also identify open problems for researchers interested in this ecosystem.

5e7ae3dc98a741e2f9b5d7b3.title_original: Analysis of Commit Signing on GitHub
5e7ae3dc98a741e2f9b5d7b3.excerpt: arXiv:2604.14014v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Since 1999, the security community has known that managing cryptographic keys is hard for users of cryptographic systems. Git lets software developers use private keys they control to digitally sign the commits that record their code changes to a repository. This practice offers a rare opportunity to study how a large community manages cryptographic keys in everyday work. In this paper, we study end-to-end commit signing, using GitHub accounts as our sampling unit. Our 2% stratified sample of the GitHub population comprises 2,737,649 accounts, 71,694 of which have made at least one commit. For these accounts, we analyze 16,112,439 commits across 874,198 repositories and collect 208,546 public keys uploaded to the sampled accounts. We examine developers' signing key usage patterns and compare our findings with those of prior commit signing studies, most of which used repository-based samples and paid less attention to key management. We then outline a path toward more usable key management for developers.

9575013c6306b1566b6fc4d0.excerpt: arXiv:2606.23496v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Discrete text-trigger optimization -- searching for text sequences that, when ingested by a model, steer it toward a specified objective -- underpins model red-teaming (e.g., LLM jailbreaks), as well as auditing and interpretability. CVE-2026-95823.description: tcp_pkt_linearize() in subsys/net/ip/tcp.c is used by th_get() whenever a received TCP header is not contiguous in a single net_buf. While pulling the header bytes out of the following fragments, the loop called net_buf_unref() on an emptied fragment without first detaching its frags pointer. net_buf_unref() walks the whole fragment list, so the payload buffers still linked behind that fragment were freed as well, and the stale pointer was then reinstalled into the packet as buf->frags, producing a use-after-free and a later double free during packet teardown. The same loop also advanced to second->frags unconditionally: when the fragment still held payload after the header remainder was pulled, it was spliced out of the packet without ever being unreferenced, permanently leaking that buffer and silently dropping the data it carried. The defect is reached from tcp_recv() via th_get() on every received TCP segment, before connection lookup or any header validation, so a single unauthenticated segment that matches a listening socket is sufficient. An attacker only needs the TCP header to straddle a net_buf boundary, which they can arrange from off-link: IPv6 extension headers are accepted on receive and their length is added to the header offset by th_get(), so a Destination Options header of a suitable length places the TCP header across the boundary of the fixed-size receive buffers (CONFIG_NET_BUF_DATA_SIZE). Packet chains assembled from several sources - IPv4/IPv6 reassembly, 6LoWPAN/802.15.4 reassembly, tunnel or virtual interfaces that strip an outer header, or drivers producing scatter-gather chains - can additionally present a short interior fragment that the loop empties exactly, which is the case that frees the remainder of the packet while it is still in use. The reliably reachable consequence is exhaustion of the receive buffer pool: each crafted segment leaks one net_buf from the fixed CONFIG_NET_BUF_RX_COUNT pool, the buffers are never reclaimed, and once the pool is empty the device can no longer receive network traffic until it is rebooted. Where a fragment is emptied exactly, the impact rises to memory corruption: freed pool buffers are written through by the remainder of the loop, their contents may be delivered to the application, and the packet is double-freed on teardown. The fix saves and clears second->frags before the net_buf_unref() so only the emptied header fragment is released, and advances to the next fragment only when second->len == 0, keeping any fragment that still holds payload in the packet. This restores the detach-before-unref ownership pattern used elsewhere in the stack, for example in net_pkt_trim_buffer().

CVE-2010-20126.description: Virtual Keyboard plugin for SquirrelMail through 0.9.1 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject script by supplying unsanitized input in the passformname parameter. Attackers can craft GET requests to /plugins/vkeyboard/vkeyboard.php with script payloads in passformname to execute code in victims' browsers and steal session cookies. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

CVE-2012-20007.description: ThinkPHP 2.0 through 2.2 and 3.0 Lite mode contains an eval injection vulnerability in the Dispatcher PATH_INFO parsing, which uses preg_replace with the /e modifier and a double-quoted replacement. Unauthenticated attackers can send crafted requests to index.php with a malicious 's' parameter containing PHP expressions to execute arbitrary code on the server. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-14.

CVE-2012-20008.description: openSIS 5.1 before 9.0 contains a local file inclusion vulnerability that allows authenticated users to include arbitrary files through the modname parameter of ajax.php. Attackers can prefix a payload with misc/ and use ../ directory traversal to read sensitive files like /etc/passwd or execute local scripts in the web server context. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

CVE-2016-20105.description: Lucee Server versions 5.0.0.0 before 5.3.4.46 contain an insecure default configuration that allows unauthenticated attackers to set the initial admin password via the first-run form on /lucee/admin/web.cfm and /lucee/admin/server.cfm. Attackers can access the 'New Password' set-password form before any password is configured to seize administrative control of the server. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-24.

CVE-2016-20106.description: NUUO NVRmini 2 through 3.0.8 contains a file disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read web-root files by passing a filename to the 'css' parameter of css_parser.php. Attackers can retrieve PHP source files confined to the document root, exposing hardcoded credentials and sensitive application logic. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-17.

CVE-2018-25442.description: Baidu UEditor 1.4.0 before 1.4.3.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to make arbitrary requests via the source[] parameter in /ueditor/jsp/controller.jsp?action=catchimage. Attackers can supply crafted URLs that the ImageHunter component fetches through url.openConnection() to reach internal services and bypass network restrictions. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2024-07-03.

CVE-2018-25443.description: Baidu UEditor 1.4.0 through 1.4.3.3 contains an unrestricted file upload vulnerability in the catchimage action of /ueditor/net/controller.ashx that only validates the Content-Type header. Unauthenticated attackers can supply a source[] URL like x.jpg?.aspx to retain a malicious extension and write an executable .aspx file for remote code execution. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-17.

CVE-2019-25782.description: ThinkPHP 5.0.0 before 5.0.24 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute commands by setting _method=__construct in POST data to overwrite the Request filter property. Attackers can send POST requests to endpoints reached via ?s=captcha or ?s=index/index/index with filter[]=system and server[REQUEST_METHOD] values to execute arbitrary system commands. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-14.

CVE-2019-25783.description: Tiny Tiny RSS before commit c68ac04 (2019-03-03) contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect users through the unvalidated 'return' parameter. Attackers can craft requests to /public.php?op=login with an absolute external URL in 'return', which is placed in the Location header to send victims to attacker-controlled sites. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2026-02-26.

CVE-2019-25784.description: FineCMS versions 5.0.4 before 5.0.11 contain an unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in the data2 API action handled by list_tag in libraries/Template.php. Attackers can send GET requests to index.php?c=api&m=data2 with a valid auth hash and the param action=sql sql='...' to execute arbitrary SELECT queries and extract database information. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-14.

CVE-2019-25785.description: FineReport 8.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files through the resourcepath parameter of the /WebReport/ReportServer endpoint. Attackers can send GET requests with op=chart and cmd=get_geo_json to read sensitive files like privilege.xml and extract admin credentials. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

CVE-2019-25786.description: Gnuboard5 5.0.1 before 5.3.3.3 and 5.4.0.1 before 5.4.0.2 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the arr_ajax_msg parameter. Attackers can craft GET requests to /plugin/sms5/ajax.sms_emoticon.php, where common.php's @extract($_GET) injects the value into the echoed JSON output, executing script in victims' browsers. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

CVE-2020-37290.description: Kiwi TCMS before 8.6 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the User.filter JSON-RPC method that allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve user account information. Attackers can send a POST request to /json-rpc/ invoking User.filter with a query parameter to disclose sensitive user data without authentication. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

CVE-2021-48021.description: Chamilo LMS 1.11.10 before 1.11.16 contains an unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in the searchOptionsFromTags function through the options parameter of extra_field.ajax.php. Attackers can send POST requests with a malicious JSON options array to inject SQL into the IN clause and extract database information. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-14.

CVE-2021-48022.description: Rocket.Chat versions 0.61.0 before 3.11.4, 3.12.x before 3.12.4 and 3.13.x before 3.13.2 contain a missing authorization vulnerability allowing unauthenticated attackers to read any room's messages via the livechat:loadHistory Meteor method. Attackers can mint a guest token through livechat:registerGuest and send POST requests to /api/v1/method.callAnon with a target rid parameter to retrieve message history without membership checks. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2025-02-13.

CVE-2021-48023.description: Weaver E-cology 9.0 contains an unrestricted file upload vulnerability in /page/exportImport/uploadOperation.jsp that allows unauthenticated attackers to upload arbitrary JSP files. Attackers can send a crafted multipart POST request with a JSP webshell written to /page/exportImport/fileTransfer/ to achieve remote code execution. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-20.

CVE-2021-48025.description: OpenSNS 3.2.1 contains an unauthenticated code injection vulnerability in the shareBox method of ShareController that allows attackers to invoke arbitrary model methods via the query parameter. Attackers can send crafted GET requests to /index.php?s=weibo/Share/shareBox abusing parse_str and ShareModel::getInfo to reach Schedule::runSchedule and execute code through assert. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-14.

CVE-2021-48026.description: Zhongqing Naboo Education Cloud Platform builds through 2021-07-09 contain a missing authentication vulnerability in the /api/TeacherQuery/SearchTeacherInSiteWithPagerRecords endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to access sensitive teacher data. Attackers can send unauthenticated GET requests to this endpoint to retrieve user names, login names, and admin ids from the JSON response. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-11-15.

CVE-2021-48027.description: OTOBO 10.0.1 before 10.0.13 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect users by supplying arbitrary URLs to the ExternalURLJump action. Attackers can craft GET requests to /otobo/index.pl?Action=ExternalURLJump with a malicious URL parameter, which the ExternalURLJump.pm module redirects to without an allow-list check, enabling phishing attacks. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

CVE-2021-48028.description: Open Journal Systems 2.1.0 before 3.0.0 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect users to external domains by abusing the source parameter. Attackers can send GET requests to /index.php/index/user/setLocale/<locale> with a source value beginning with '@', which UserHandler.inc.php appends to the server host, redirecting victims to attacker-controlled sites for phishing. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2024-12-05.

CVE-2022-51027.description: MeterSphere versions 1.13.0 before 1.14.7 and 1.15.0 before 1.16.4 contain a pre-authentication code injection vulnerability due to the /plugin/** endpoints being exposed with anonymous access. Attackers can upload a malicious jar via POST /plugin/add and invoke it through POST /plugin/customMethod using the 'entry' and 'request' parameters, which are passed to Class.forName and method invocation for remote code execution. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-14.

CVE-2022-51028.description: CmsEasy 7.7.5_20210919 contains an unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in the execsql_action function at /?case=crossall&act=execsql that executes attacker-supplied queries decrypted with the hardcoded key 'cmseasy_sql'. Attackers can send a crafted 'sql' parameter to run arbitrary SQL and dump the admin username and password hash. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-22.

CVE-2022-51029.description: Synway SMG Gateway Management Software builds through 2022-03-15 contain a path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files via the downfile parameter in /down.php. Attackers can send a multipart POST request to /down.php with a traversal path in downfile to retrieve sensitive files like /etc/passwd. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-20.

CVE-2022-51030.description: QiboCMS V7 contains an arbitrary file download vulnerability in inc/job/download.php that allows unauthenticated attackers to read files by supplying a base64-encoded url parameter to /do/job.php?job=download. Attackers can bypass the .php extension check using the Windows 'ph<' wildcard to download sensitive files such as configuration files containing database credentials. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-18.

CVE-2022-51031.description: PMB 7.3.1 before 7.3.15 and 7.4.x before 7.4.5 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject script through unescaped POST parameter names. Attackers can send crafted parameter names to opac_css/index.php extended_search, which empr.inc.php and languages.inc.php reflect into hidden form inputs to execute JavaScript. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

CVE-2022-51032.description: Reddit Top RSS through commit 5e38bfd contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the unescaped score GET parameter. Attackers can craft links with a score value that closes the input value attribute in html.php, executing JavaScript in victims' browsers. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

CVE-2022-51033.description: JoomBri Careers 3.3.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the 'keyword' parameter of the /for-jobseekers/search-jobs endpoint in com_jbcareers. Attackers can craft malicious URLs using an attribute-breakout payload with onfocus and autofocus to execute arbitrary JavaScript and steal session tokens or credentials. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

CVE-2022-51034.description: Tangshan Pingsheng Reservoir Safety Supervision Platform builds through 2022-11-30 contain an unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in the simcardId parameter of /WebServices/SIMMaintainService.asmx/GetAllRechargeRecordsBySIMCardId. Attackers can send crafted POST requests with time-based MSSQL payloads to extract database information including user, version, and database name. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2024-07-30.

CVE-2022-51035.description: SLiMS Senayan Library Management System 9.4.0 before 9.4.2 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the destination parameter of /index.php?p=member, which is echoed unmodified into the login form action attribute. Unauthenticated attackers can craft a malicious destination value to inject script and hijack PHPSESSID sessions of victims who access the link. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

CVE-2023-54416.description: Tiki Wiki CMS Groupware 12.12 through 12.14, 15.5 before 18.10, 19.0 before 21.9, 22.0 before 24.3, and 25.0 contain a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the objectId parameter of tiki-ajax_services.php. Attackers can send a crafted GET request with the comment controller and list action to execute arbitrary JavaScript and steal session tokens or credentials. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

CVE-2023-54417.description: Nuxt 3.0.0 before 3.4.2 contains a semi-arbitrary file read vulnerability in the vite-node dev server middleware that allows unauthenticated attackers to read files by supplying an absolute path as the moduleId. Attackers can send GET requests to /__nuxt_vite_node__/module/ with an absolute file path to read sensitive system files. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

CVE-2023-54418.description: Nuxt 3.0.0-rc.1 before 3.0.0-rc.13 contains an arbitrary file read vulnerability caused by the Vite dev server default setting vite.server.fs.strict=false. Unauthenticated attackers can request /_nuxt/@fs/<absolute path> with a raw query to read arbitrary files like /etc/passwd from the system. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-18.

CVE-2023-54419.description: nginxWebUI 3.0.0 before 3.5.8 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to reach the /AdminPage/conf/runCmd endpoint by using a case-variant path that evades the case-sensitive /adminPage/ login filter. Attackers can pass OS commands through the cmd parameter, which are executed via /bin/sh with insufficient filtering of & and $() characters, achieving remote code execution. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-14.

CVE-2023-54420.description: LiveBOS builds through 2023-08-16 contain a path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files via the imgName parameter in /feed/ShowImage.do using a ';.js.jsp' suffix bypass. Attackers can send crafted GET requests with directory traversal sequences in imgName to read system files such as /etc/passwd. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-30.

CVE-2023-54421.description: phpLDAPadmin 1.1.0 before 1.2.5 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the dn parameter of cmd.php?cmd=template_engine. Attackers can supply an unparseable dn value that pretty_print_dn returns unescaped in the 'No such entry' error, executing JavaScript in victims' browsers. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

CVE-2023-54422.description: iDocView before 13.10.1_20231115 contains an unrestricted file upload vulnerability in the /html/2word endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to write arbitrary files by supplying a malicious url parameter. Attackers can send a crafted GET request with the url parameter to download linked resources with an unsanitized path and unblocked .jsp extension, achieving remote code execution. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-11-22.

CVE-2024-58401.description: Bagisto 2.1.0 before 2.2.1 contains a client-side template injection vulnerability in the search page where the 'query' parameter is rendered unescaped inside a Vue app root. Unauthenticated attackers can send crafted VueJS template expressions to the /bagisto-common/search endpoint via the 'query' parameter to execute arbitrary JavaScript in victims' browsers. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2024-07-30.

CVE-2024-58402.description: Azon Dominator releases through 2024-06-03 contain an SQL injection vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to manipulate database queries through the cid parameter in /fetch_products.php. Attackers can send crafted POST requests with boolean-based or time-based blind payloads to extract sensitive database information. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2024-07-30.

CVE-2024-58403.description: AnyShare builds through 2024-11 contain a missing authentication vulnerability in the /api/ShareMgnt/Usrm_GetAllUsers endpoint that exposes user records including password fields. Attackers can send unauthenticated POST requests with a [start,limit] body to retrieve usernames, passwords, and department information for all users. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2024-12-25.

CVE-2026-113425.description: When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as a mail proxy, undisclosed traffic can cause a use-after-free in an nginx worker process. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR. Impact: A remote unauthenticated attacker may crash an nginx worker process or corrupt its memory, disrupting service. Remote code execution is a potential impact. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-116443.description: Dell PowerStore SDNAS contains a stack-based buffer overflow in the NAS TFTP service that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause a denial of service or potential code execution.

CVE-2026-116449.description: Dell PowerStore SDNAS contains an OS Command Injection vulnerability that could allow an attacker with internal network access to execute arbitrary commands as root on the NAS node.

CVE-2026-116953.description: Description: When an iRule that processes client traffic using the GENERICMESSAGE::route command is configured on a virtual server, undisclosed requests can cause the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to terminate and may lead to remote code execution (RCE). Impact: Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts. This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the BIG-IP system and may allow the attacker to perform RCE. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-118899.description: When using the listen directive with the ssl parameter in the http block with TLSv1.3 enabled, an attacker can use a specially crafted TLS connection to cause an infinite loop in the NGINX worker process while reading the HTTP request body. As a result, the worker process stops accepting new connections and processing existing connections. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated. Impact: This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) of NGINX. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-120049.description: The Link Library plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'linkfile[name]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.10.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires an administrator to have enabled the "Link File" option within the plugin's settings, which activates the vulnerable file upload field on the public add-link form.

CVE-2026-120285.description: Description When an HTTP profile and an iRule containing the PSC::ip_address command are configured on a virtual server, undisclosed requests can cause the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to terminate and may lead to remote code execution (RCE). Impact Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts. This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the BIG-IP system and may allow the attacker to perform RCE. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-120292.description: Description: When an HTTP profile and an iRule using the MR::message route command are configured on a virtual server, undisclosed requests can cause the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to terminate and may lead to remote code execution (RCE) Impact: Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts. This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the BIG-IP system and may allow the attacker to perform RCE. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-120718.description: Description: BIG-IP iControl REST tokens may not expire as expected in all scenarios. Impact: An attacker who has obtained a token may be able to extend its expiry lifetime unless the token owner deletes it. There is no data plane exposure; this is a control plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-120722.description: Description: When an iRule that processes client traffic using the DNS::scrape command is configured on a virtual server, undisclosed requests can cause the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to terminate and may lead to remote code execution (RCE). Impact: Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts. This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the BIG-IP system. In addition, the attacker may be able to perform RCE. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-120967.description: When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to require client certificates ("ssl_verify_client on") in a non-default stream virtual server, a remote attacker could bypass verification of client certificates. Impact: An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to bypass verification of client certificates. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-120993.description: When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use the ngx_stream_ssl_module module with dynamic certificate loading and the ngx_stream_proxy_module module with the proxy_protocol v2 directive, an abbreviated SSL handshake can cause a worker process to terminate. Impact: This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system. This is a data plane vulnerability only; there is no control plane exposure. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-121805.description: Description: When an iRule that processes client traffic using the PEM::subscriber command is configured on a virtual server, undisclosed requests can cause the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to terminate and may lead to remote code execution (RCE). Impact: Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts. This vulnerability allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the BIG-IP system and may perform RCE. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-121810.description: Description: This issue affects NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/3. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can cause a use-after-free condition in the NGINX worker process, leading to a restart. Exploitation also depends on conditions beyond the attacker’s control. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR. Impact: This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or to possibly trigger a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-121812.description: Description: When BIG-IP APM is provisioned, and a virtual server is configured with an APM access profile and a per-request policy, and the tmm.access.policytrace database key is enabled, undisclosed requests can cause the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to terminate. The key is disabled by default. Impact: Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts. This vulnerability allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the BIG-IP system . There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-123007.description: This issue affects NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/2. When NGINX processes undisclosed traffic, the flow control window can exceed the allowed threshold, potentially resulting in a heap buffer overflow typically followed by an NGINX worker segmentation fault. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR. Impact: An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or potentially execute code remotely. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-123633.description: When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use HTTP/2 for client connections and proxy client requests to a backend, a specially crafted request can result in use-after-free in the worker process, if this process is running low on worker_connections. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR. Impact: This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or may allow a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-123634.description: This issue occurs when NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as a proxy, the proxied server name includes variables, and a Server Side Includes (SSI) or mirror directive sends a subrequest to a location that resolves the same server name. Under these conditions, a specially crafted HTTP request may cause a use-after-free condition in a worker process. An attacker may also be able to execute code if Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) is disabled or the attacker can bypass ASLR. Impact: An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or perform remote code execution (RCE) Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-123637.description: When BIG-IP APM is provisioned and a per-request policy that includes the Client Information agent and Endpoint Security agents is applied to a virtual server, undisclosed requests can cause the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to terminate and may lead to remote code execution (RCE). Impact: Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts. This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the BIG-IP system and may allow the attacker to perform RCE. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-123640.description: Description When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured with the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module module, a specially crafted ClientHello message from an unauthenticated attacker causes forged values of the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module variables, affecting virtual server selection. In addition, it may also cause a disagreement with a proxied server terminating the SSL/TLS connection without Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.3 support. Impact This vulnerability may allow an attacker to forge values of the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module variables and bypass the NGINX systems stream routing segmentation. As a result, the attacker may be able to route the connection to a privileged or internal backend that should be unreachable and gain access to sensitive information. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-124990.description: The Masteriyo LMS – LMS Course Builder, Quizzes & Certificates plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in versions up to, and including, 3.5.1 via deserialization of untrusted input in the course importer. The set_post_metas() method calls maybe_unserialize() on attacker-controlled postmeta string values parsed from the uploaded JSON import file. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary PHP Objects. Exploitation by unauthenticated attackers requires that the site has enable_instructor_registration=true AND enable_guest_checkout=true AND at least one purchasable course exists. Install.php sets enable_instructor_registration=false on fresh installs, so this is a non-default configuration. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with author-level access and above.

CVE-2026-125272.description: Description: When BIG-IP APM is licensed and provisioned, and a virtual server with the APM access profile is configured with a per-request policy containing a form-based Logon Page, undisclosed requests can cause the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to terminate. Impact: Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts. This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the BIG-IP system. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-125274.description: An authenticated iControl SOAP user with at least Guest access can inject an unauthorized management request. Impact: This vulnerability may allow an authenticated attacker with network access and at least Guest role privileges to the iControl SOAP utility to execute arbitrary system commands, create or delete files, or disable services. There is no data plane exposure; this is a control plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-125283.description: When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use the try_files and alias directives with a map variable, certain combinations of regular expression captures in map and try_files can cause a segmentation fault in an NGINX worker process. Impact: An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to cause an NGINX worker process to terminate unexpectedly. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-125806.description: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in WP Media WP Rocket wp-rocket allows Stored XSS.This issue affects WP Rocket: from n/a before 3.24.1.

CVE-2026-126336.description: Description: When BIG-IP APM is provisioned and a virtual server is configured with an APM Access profile and a SAML Service Provider (SP) agent with encrypted assertions enabled, undisclosed requests can cause the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to terminate. Impact: Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts. This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the BIG-IP system. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-126699.description: The Majestic Support – The Leading-Edge Help Desk & Customer Support Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'mjsupport_message' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.2.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that a staff member or administrator opens the affected ticket and clicks the attacker-planted link on the ticket-detail screen, as the VenoBox payload is triggered on click rather than on page load. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

CVE-2026-126721.description: The Magic Login Mail or QR Code plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation via Administrator Account Takeover in versions up to, and including, 2.07. This is due to the `curpageurl()` function falling back to the raw `$_SERVER['HTTP_HOST']` value — with no validation against the site's configured origin via `home_url()` or `site_url()` — when `get_the_permalink()` returns empty or false, allowing an attacker-controlled Host header to become the URL origin of the magic-login link generated by `generate_url()` and delivered to the target via `wp_mail()`. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to intercept the one-time uid and token pair sent to a targeted Administrator's email and replay them against the real site, causing `autologin_via_url()` to call `wp_set_auth_cookie()` and establish a full Administrator session on the targeted account. Exploitation requires the `[magic_login]` shortcode to render on a path where `get_the_permalink()` returns empty or false (such as a 404 page or a block-theme header template part), the web server to forward non-canonical Host headers, the attacker to know the target administrator's email address, and the administrator to click the attacker-originated magic-login link. Successful exploitation gives the attacker control of a distinct, already-privileged Administrator account; it does not promote the attacker's original account. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

CVE-2026-126751.description: Retool versions 3.253.0 before 3.253.19, 3.254.0 before 3.284.12, and 3.285.0 before 3.300.4 contain a DOM-based cross-site scripting vulnerability in the custom-component-collections.html postMessage handler that imports received code without origin validation. Unauthenticated attackers can send crafted postMessage events that load attacker-controlled code via data:text/javascript URIs to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's context. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2026-04-22.

CVE-2026-126752.description: Dagu 1.23.0 before 2.0.0 defaults auth.mode to none, allowing unauthenticated attackers to execute OS commands through the /api/v2/dag-runs endpoint. Attackers can send a POST request with an inline spec defining steps containing arbitrary shell commands to achieve remote code execution. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2026-03-11.

CVE-2026-126753.description: LimeSurvey 6.5.0 before 6.16.11 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect users by supplying arbitrary values to the url parameter. Attackers can send crafted GET requests to index.php?r=editorLink, where EditorLinkController concatenates url and route unvalidated, redirecting victims to attacker-controlled sites for phishing. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2026-03-20.

CVE-2026-126754.description: cPanel & WHM 11.134.0.13 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the mpidentity parameter of /mailman/listinfo. Attackers can send crafted requests with a script-context breakout payload in mpidentity to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2026-06-08.

CVE-2026-126755.description: ArangoDB before 3.12.11 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability caused by a parser differential between the raw path authentication gate and the URL-decoded dispatch logic. Attackers can send requests with a %5f-encoded leading underscore to endpoints like /_db/_system/%5fapi/simple/first-example to reach /_api/* actions as superuser without authentication. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2026-09-16.

CVE-2026-126822.description: Description: When BIG-IP APM is provisioned, an Access Profile is configured as a SAML SP (Service Provider) and is applied to a virtual server, undisclosed requests can cause the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to terminate. Impact: Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts. This vulnerability allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the BIG-IP system. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-127178.description: A stored cross site scripting attack when viewing email aliases in postfixadmin 4.0 before 4.0.7, and postfixadmin 3.3 before 3.3.17 could be caused by signed in admins able to inject aliases.

CVE-2026-128719.description: An issue in PHPGurukul Employee Leaves Management System (ELMS) Version 2.1 allows a remote attacker to escalate privileges via the password recovery functionality

CVE-2026-132222.description: BizPrint (print-google-cloud-print-gcp-woocommerce) before 4.10.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in its Debug\Core component that allows any authenticated user, including the lowest-privilege Subscriber role, to invoke the getPrinters and sendPrintRequest AJAX actions without a nonce or capability check. Attackers can send a crafted admin-ajax.php request with an arbitrary WooCommerce order_id to dispatch print jobs for other customers' orders and disclose printer configuration, exposing cross-customer PII and abusing printer resources.

CVE-2026-132224.description: Optimizely Web Experimentation before 2026-11-17 mishandles the account signup flow, leading to presence of attacker-controlled code in the projectJS (aka Project JavaScript) field of certain cdn.optimizely.com assets.

CVE-2026-30502.description: A Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in OpenKM v6.3.12 allows attackers to execute arbitrary Javascript in the context of the user's browser via a crafted input injected into the Content parameter.

CVE-2026-48728.description: The GLPI Inventory Plugin handles network discovery, inventory, software deployment, and data collection for GLPI agents. Prior to 1.6.8, the /b/deploy, /b/collect, and /b/esx agent API endpoints do not authenticate requests before processing Deploy, Collect, and ESX task operations. An unauthenticated remote attacker can enumerate jobs and manipulate their status through these endpoints, disclosing job information and interfering with task processing. This issue is fixed in version 1.6.8.

CVE-2026-63189.description: Dialoqbase is an application for creating chatbots. Prior to 1.11.5, the unauthenticated GET /api/v1/view/* route in server/src/routes/api/v1/view/root.ts resolves its attacker-controlled wildcard path without normalization or containment, allowing traversal outside the intended uploads directory and arbitrary server file reads. Reading environment files can disclose DB_SECRET_KEY, the application’s JWT signing key, which permits forged administrator tokens and takeover of bots, conversations, integrations, and stored third-party credentials. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.5.

CVE-2026-71861.description: The Chainguard SDK is a public Go SDK for integrating with the Chainguard platform. Prior to 0.1.107, auth/aws.VerifyToken trusts the Chainguard-Audience and Chainguard-Identity headers without requiring those headers to be covered by AWS SigV4 SignedHeaders. An attacker with a fresh STS GetCallerIdentity request signed by a victim can rewrite the unsigned binding headers and replay the proof to another relying party, causing the relying party to authenticate the victim’s AWS identity for an attacker-chosen audience and identity. Code that only uses auth/aws.GenerateToken is unaffected because the generator signs the binding headers, and exploitation requires a signed request within its validity window. This issue is fixed in version 0.1.107.

CVE-2025-64441.description: The ownCloud Desktop Client synchronizes files between an ownCloud server and a desktop. Prior to 6.0.2, an authenticated attacker can share a specially crafted file with a victim. If the file is synced by the client and revealed in the macOS Finder, it can cause operating-system command injection on the victim’s computer. This issue is fixed in version 6.0.2.

CVE-2026-109909.description: A out of bounds read after using negative integers during offset calculation during PCF decoding in X.Org libXfont before 2.0.10 could be used by authenticated X clients to crash the X server or expose sensitive information in its memory.

CVE-2026-112160.description: In PcVue version 17.0.0 through 17.0.1 included, user account security settings could be modified. This could lead to unauthorized modification of password policies or other security-related account settings by privileged users. The update aligns user account management with the existing security-altering enforcement model and prevents unauthorized security configuration changes.

CVE-2026-116441.description: Dell PowerStore SDNAS contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the storage-processor interconnect driver that could allow a malicious peer to execute code with system privileges.

CVE-2026-116442.description: Dell PowerStore SDNAS contains an authentication-bypass-by-replay vulnerability in the NAS NDMP service that could allow a network attacker to gain backup and restore control of the appliance.

CVE-2026-121591.description: Mattermost Desktop App versions <=6.3 6.0.3 6.3.2.0 fail to bound the Calls widget resize dimensions before applying them to the window, which allows a configured Mattermost server to terminate the Desktop App process via a crafted resizeCallsWidget IPC message sent from the Calls widget window. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00787

CVE-2026-126675.description: Incorrect default permissions in Nitro PDF Pro before 26.4 on Windows allow a local low-privileged user to execute code in the context of another user who launches the application.

CVE-2026-130007.description: k8s-mcp-server manages Kubernetes clusters through the Model Context Protocol. Prior to 1.1.0, SERVER_MODE defaults to SSE, with the listener on 0.0.0.0:8080, but main.go creates the SSE server without an authentication option or context function. The GET /sse handler creates a sessionId that is only a correlation value, and the POST /message handler accepts a loadable sessionId without an authorization or Origin check before dispatching tools/call; consequently, any client able to reach the port can enumerate and invoke registered Kubernetes tools without credentials. Read-only mode is disabled by default, leaving write-capable Kubernetes tools available to run with the server's configured cluster privileges. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.0.

CVE-2026-130008.description: sqlite-mcp is a Model Context Protocol server for SQLite. Prior to 0.1.2, the default read-only mode can be bypassed through execute_query, which accepts a leading SELECT while the SQLite driver executes trailing statements, and through describe_table, which interpolates the caller-controlled table_name into PRAGMA table_info. Either path can issue ATTACH DATABASE, which opens an attached file read-write despite mode=ro and can make the protected database writable, read other SQLite database files, or create a SQLite-format file at a path writable by the server process. Existing non-empty files that are not SQLite databases are refused and left unchanged. The server has no built-in authentication and listens on all interfaces at :8080 by default, so any client that can reach the port can invoke these tools unless an authenticating proxy is in place. This issue is fixed in version 0.1.2.

CVE-2026-130154.description: Zyrabit Platform provides sovereign AI infrastructure for enterprise retrieval-augmented generation. Prior to 2.4.4, import_to_vault(source_path, destination_name) accepts both caller-controlled paths, but the content-pattern guard does not confine destination_name. The vulnerable tool is implemented in zyrabit-slm/api-rag/app/domain/services/mcp_service.py, where Path(DOCS_DIR) / destination_name is passed to shutil.copy2, allowing traversal or an absolute destination to write outside the vault. An unrestricted source_path can be copied into the vault and retrieved through secure_query, disclosing files readable by the service; files that do not match the executable-pattern filter pass that filter. When ENABLE_LEGACY_EXTENSIONS=true, zyrabit-slm/api-rag/app/main.py registers POST /mcp/rpc without get_current_user, allowing unauthenticated network tool calls; this optional exposure is disabled by default and is not required for local invocation. If an attacker can stage chosen source content and write to an execution-triggered destination, the advisory describes conditional process execution. This issue is fixed in version 2.4.4.

CVE-2026-130156.description: Bazarr is a companion application to Sonarr and Radarr. Prior to 1.6.3-beta.11, the /api/subtitles/subtitles-info handler uses SubtitleNameContents.get() in subtitles_contents.py and reads the caller-supplied subtitlePath after checking only its subtitle extension; because the resolved path is not confined to files indexed by Bazarr, traversal can read files outside the media library. The /api/subtitles/subtitles handler in subtitles.py passes caller-supplied path and reference to sync and translation without per-path authorization, allowing an out-of-library reference file to be read and output to overwrite a file outside the media library. The authenticate decorator gates both endpoints when API authentication is enabled, while auth = None allows access without credentials. Both paths can affect only files that the Bazarr process can read or write. This issue is fixed in version 1.6.3-beta.11.

CVE-2026-132219.description: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability. Exploiting this vulnerability allows a user to view the names of other users/companies on the platform by iterating over the numerical value that identifies the customer in 'DocumentosOpcionesImprimir' parameter in'/Gestion/DocumentosOpcionesImprimir/'.

CVE-2026-132220.description: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in winCRM. Exploiting this vulnerability could allow a remote user to send a specially crafted URL to the victim and steal their session data by allowing JavaScript code to be injected in 'Tarea' parameter in '/Tareas/TareasCrear?ddv=cal'.

CVE-2026-132231.description: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 remote code execution was possible via best-fit character mapping in Perforce settings

CVE-2026-132232.description: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 remote code execution was possible via argument injection in Perforce settings

CVE-2026-132233.description: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 remote code execution was possible via build attribute injection

CVE-2026-132234.description: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 remote code execution was possible via argument injection in Mercurial VCS root settings

CVE-2026-132235.description: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 remote code execution was possible via path traversal in project import archives

CVE-2026-132236.description: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 remote code execution was possible via path traversal in the pipeline YAML file path

CVE-2026-132237.description: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 remote code execution was possible via path traversal in the external artifact cache

CVE-2026-132238.description: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.8 disclosure of password parameter values to project viewers was possible

CVE-2026-132239.description: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 missing authorization in the Kubernetes integration allowed project viewers to use stored credentials

CVE-2026-132240.description: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 XXE via Maven settings file upload was possible

CVE-2026-132241.description: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 XXE in the .NET build steps auto-discovery was possible

CVE-2026-132242.description: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 stored XSS in the Promote build dialog was possible

CVE-2026-132243.description: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 stored XSS on the Docker Container Info tab was possible

CVE-2026-132244.description: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 stored XSS on the Disk Usage and Build Time pages was possible

CVE-2026-132245.description: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 DoS via agent command results was possible

CVE-2026-132246.description: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 privilege escalation to system administrator was possible after disabling per-project permissions

CVE-2026-132247.description: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 improper authorization allowed viewing build process details via agent stacktraces

CVE-2026-132248.description: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3 improper authorization allowed project viewers to change project IDs

CVE-2026-132249.description: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 stored XSS in the Shared Resources build feature was possible

CVE-2026-132250.description: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3 privilege escalation was possible via Basic authentication with a restricted access token

CVE-2026-132251.description: In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3 privilege escalation was possible by issuing new tokens from a restricted access token

CVE-2026-16021.description: Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to bound the resources consumed while processing an uploaded custom emoji image which allows an authenticated user with default permissions to make the server unresponsive for all users via repeated custom emoji uploads.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00720

CVE-2026-16050.description: Mattermost versions 11.7.x <= 11.7.11 fail to sanitize channel mentions when rendering permalinked posts, which allows an authenticated user to discover the display names of private channels they do not have access to via a permalink to a post that mentions the channel.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00721

CVE-2026-17537.description: Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to enforce the channel Access Control Policy's file download permission check when serving file metadata and thumbnails through the drafts, scheduled posts, and post edit history endpoints, which allows an authenticated user who has lost eligibility under the policy to view metadata and thumbnails of file attachments via those endpoints, even though direct file access is correctly denied. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00740

CVE-2026-17575.description: Mattermost versions 11.8.x <= 11.8.5, 11.7.x <= 11.7.10, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fails to validate the type of card property fields which allows a board Editor to make a board or card permanently unopenable for all users via a crafted PATCH request storing a non-string property name or value.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00743

CVE-2026-18045.description: Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to enforce the MFA requirement on the update and delete user endpoints, which allows an authenticated user who has not configured MFA to modify or delete their own account via the API despite system-wide MFA enforcement being enabled. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00744

CVE-2026-18075.description: Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to invalidate cached WebSocket session state when an OAuth app is deleted, which allows a revoked OAuth integration to keep receiving real-time events, including private channel posts, via a WebSocket connection that was already open when the app was deleted.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00745

CVE-2026-18079.description: Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 Fail to revoke a user's active sessions when a bulk import links an existing user account to a bot record or changes the account's auth_service/auth_data, which allows an attacker in possession of a session token issued before the import to retain full authenticated access to the affected account via a system administrator-triggered bulk import job.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00746
