f73f513a6a144a200822c09a.title_original: DetectViT: Test-time Backdoor Detection for Vision Transformers via Inter-Head Attention Discrepancy
f73f513a6a144a200822c09a.excerpt: arXiv:2611.23770v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) now underpin the visual encoders of most multimodal models, but this success comes at a cost: relying on third-party pretrained checkpoints leaves these systems open to backdoor attacks. Existing test-time detection methods rely on either the predicted label or intermediate embeddings, limiting their applicability across diverse tasks and incurring substantial computational overhead. In this work, we study how backdoor triggers affect the multi-head attention mechanism of ViTs and identify two distinct anomalous patterns: $\textit{complete attention hijacking}$, causing the attention to exhibit abnormally high inter-head spatial overlap, and $\textit{partial attention hijacking}$, causing an abnormally large variance in the concentration of the attention distribution. Motivated by these findings, we propose $\textbf{DetectViT}$, a test-time backdoor detection method that requires neither training data, model outputs, nor any prior knowledge of the trigger. DetectViT quantifies the two hijacking phenomena via an inter-head consistency score and an inter-head entropy variance score, with thresholds estimated from a small out-of-distribution (OOD) calibration set drawn from an arbitrary source. Across four representative attacks, diverse architectures (DeiT, CLIP, and LLaVA), and downstream tasks (image classification and captioning), DetectViT substantially outperforms all baselines with as few as 64--

8a97b744a858122914ae26d1.title_original: RECLAIM: Robot-Vision-Informed Adversarial Patch Defense via Embodied Attention Feedback
8a97b744a858122914ae26d1.excerpt: arXiv:2611.24494v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language-action policies control embodied agents through a perception-action loop grounded in physical interaction, where adversarial patches can corrupt action predictions and thereby alter subsequent observations. To mitigate these threats, many existing defenses rely on policy adaptation or auxiliary models, but require additional training or inference. We introduce RECLAIM, a training-free, inference-time defense that uses a frozen VLA's own attention response to local visual interventions to guide purification during closed-loop embodied manipulation. Our key insight is that attention changes induced by local edits provide feedback for choosing where and how to purify as the robot interacts with its environment. RECLAIM combines this feedback with robot geometry to refine patch localization and select local treatments, then revalidates them as the agent's embodied actions change the observed scene. We evaluate RECLAIM against patches generated by four adversarial attack methods across multiple manipulation task suites under frozen VLA control. Under adversarial patch attacks, RECLAIM succeeds in at least one rollout on 95% of the evaluated tasks and raises rollout success on LIBERO-Object from 0% without defense to 70.0%. fd631a0eb8a2c8d8641c0fce.title_original: SCR: Detecting Backdoor-Poisoned Samples through Clean-Reference Residuals
fd631a0eb8a2c8d8641c0fce.excerpt: arXiv:2611.24558v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep neural networks are vulnerable to backdoor attacks, in which adversaries manipulate model predictions by injecting poisoned samples into training data. Detecting these samples remains challenging because legitimate semantic variation can obscure poisoning-related signals in learned representations. Consequently, class-level statistics used by existing detectors may flag benign feature deviations while overlooking poisoned samples that blend into the class distribution. In this paper, we propose Semantic Counterfactual Residualization (SCR), which uses a small set of clean reference samples to account for benign variation through sample-specific feature reconstruction. SCR identifies poisoned samples by detecting coherent deviations from these clean baselines, without requiring prior knowledge of the attacks. We evaluate SCR through experiments covering twelve dirty-label and clean-label attacks across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny ImageNet. With a small clean-reference set, SCR achieves attack-averaged true positive rates above 99.5\% and false positive rates below 2\% on each dataset, outperforming eight representative detection baselines in macro-TPR.

3e74f0a0021dbfd605b02ad4.title_original: Stealing Exact Training Data from Other Clients during Federated Learning
3e74f0a0021dbfd605b02ad4.excerpt: arXiv:2611.24689v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Malicious adversaries can employ gradient inversion attacks to reverse-engineer private data using the model updates of a round in Federated Learning. While there have been developments in gradient inversion for text, exact text recovery by a malicious client has so far remained infeasible, as FedAvg entangles the gradient contributions of many clients and obscures the signal of any individual sentence. We introduce a novel attack pipeline that unwinds this entanglement progressively through an iterative loop, in which the gradient contributions of sentences recovered exactly in one round are subtracted from the aggregate, exposing the remaining sentences for recovery in the next iteration. We show, for the first time, exact sentence recovery, with 100% precision, and on aggregates containing up to $4\times$ more tokens than the model's hidden dimension, we recover up to 80.2% of client sentences exactly, a regime where existing attacks recover none exactly.

2ec7f0e5d0c02bb64ee49888.title_original: "I Don't Think It's a Scam": A First Look at Family Intervention Barriers in Elder Abuse Discussions on Reddit and Baidu Tieba
2ec7f0e5d0c02bb64ee49888.excerpt: arXiv:2611.24899v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When older adults trust scammers despite warnings, families face obstacles to intervention. Complainants aged 60 and older reported \$4.9 billion in losses in 2024 to the U.S. Internet Crime Complaint Center. In Reddit posts recording reactions, account locks or credential changes appeared in 8.9\% under resistance or continued involvement, compared with 33.3\% under acceptance. Measures such as phone or network monitoring and financial takeover were reported more often under resistance. eb713f0e39d52ae61e52ea0f.title_original: Static Attribution of Android Residential Proxy Malware Using Graph Kernels
eb713f0e39d52ae61e52ea0f.excerpt: arXiv:2604.27302v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Android residential proxy applications represent a growing class of potentially-unwanted programs (PUPs) that covertly route third-party traffic through end-user devices, enabling ad fraud, credential abuse, and evasion of geolocation controls by sophisticated threat actors. To support explainability, we map classifier decisions to automatically generated Yara rules, achieving per-family accuracies up to 88.45\% after filtering non-discriminative signatures. Finally, we discuss these results in the context of the broader ecosystem. We find that from the expanded dataset, the majority of applications (51.4\%) still available through APKPure still contain embedded proxy SDK code. 5b11d58b76b25affe41e9df4.title_original: Is Randomness Necessary for Adaptive Data Analysis?
5b11d58b76b25affe41e9df4.excerpt: arXiv:2607.07085v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Adaptive Data Analysis (ADA) problem formalizes the challenge of preventing false discovery and overfitting when a dataset is repeatedly reused. Formally, our input is a dataset containing $n$ i.i.d. samples from an unknown distribution $\mathcal{P}$ over a domain $\mathcal{X}$, and our goal is to answer a sequence of $k$ adaptively chosen statistical queries with respect to $\mathcal{P}$. The main question is how many queries we can support (i.e., how large $k$ can be), primarily as a function of the number of samples $n$. This question has been intensively studied and is relatively well-understood for randomized mechanisms: there are computationally efficient mechanisms that support $k \approx n^2$ queries, and no computationally efficient mechanism can answer $k \gg n^2$ queries. In this paper, we address a fundamental question: is randomness necessary for ADA? Despite a decade of work on ADA, this question remains open. A folklore observation dating back to the initial works on ADA is that randomness is {\em not} necessary when the analyst is computationally bounded. Yet, the necessity of randomness against computationally unbounded analysts has remained elusive. Our main contribution resolves this gap in the information-theoretic setting. Perhaps surprisingly, we show that randomness is {\em strictly necessary} to answer a non-trivial number of adaptive queries: when the analyst is unbounded, any deterministic mecha

0750b25c2ec0cd3a81c3349f.title_original: Language Model Security Modules: Turning LLM Interpretability into Runtime Defense
0750b25c2ec0cd3a81c3349f.excerpt: arXiv:2608.25697v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are served behind layered defenses such as alignment and guardrail models, yet jailbreaks still get through. Interpretability research looks inside the model, where methods such as probes and sparse autoencoders expose signals of harmful content during generation. A signal alone, however, is not a defense. To become one, the serving system must tie each signal to the right request, apply the policy as declared, and release output only when the policy allows. Today, defenses built on such signals handle these duties on their own, so every new detector needs its own integration. Yet none of these duties depends on how a signal is computed. We present Language Model Security Modules (LMSM), which adapts the design of Linux Security Modules to LLM serving and carries out these duties once in a shared mediation path. The path hosts pluggable backends that turn model internals into evidence and policies that decide what that evidence allows. Each policy declares the evidence and evaluations it needs, and LMSM provides exactly these for each request and verifies that they took place, so a failure is never mistaken for permission. Protection therefore remains cheap and correct under common serving optimizations. d0e5013e245d342ea70f1fca.title_original: Threshold Choice, Not Sample Size, Bounds Trustless Verification of Nondeterministic Compound AI Workflows
d0e5013e245d342ea70f1fca.excerpt: arXiv:2609.10601v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Compound AI pipelines chain LLM calls, retrievers, and tools and are nondeterministic: sampling, model updates, and volatile tool responses make one input yield different outputs across runs. Such pipelines increasingly run across edge, cloud, and orbital nodes owned by no single party, whose optimizations discard intermediate results before inspection. Verifying reproduction there means tolerating nondeterministic outputs, a node that may not report honestly, and intermittent access to any shared record; existing work addresses at most two at once. We give a protocol covering all three: it commits digests of each stage's inputs, outputs, and context under a policy digest pinning the metric and threshold, anchors them without trusting the executing node, defers under partition, and decides a challenge on the median of $k$ re-executions, with no quorum. Where that procedure breaks is the main result. On a synthetic HotpotQA pipeline a calibrated fixed threshold accepts 44 of 45 honest reproductions and rejects 104 of 105 divergent pairs, yet lets same-input fabrication through in 27 of 29 trials at k=5, more samples being no help since sampling sharpens an estimate without moving it. Holding that metric and this pipeline's re-execution spread fixed, the binding constraint is the threshold rather than the sample size: one derived per execution detects 19 of 29 where the best constant matched to the same zero honest rejections

fda45d52a4e1781ffb40c731.title_original: PoCoFL: A Framework for POlicy-COmpliant Federated Learning
fda45d52a4e1781ffb40c731.excerpt: arXiv:2610.03650v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a privacy-oriented learning paradigm that enables collaborative model training while keeping training data local to clients. However, FL does not guarantee that clients submit policy-compliant contributions or that aggregators process admitted contributions correctly. Update-magnitude bounds alone cannot ensure compliance with learning-specific requirements involving private data, intermediate models, or retained state. These requirements differ across FL settings, motivating a unified framework to specify and verify client and aggregation policies. This work introduces PoCoFL, a policy-compliant federated learning framework that separates three aspects: (i) FL type, (ii) policy semantics, and (iii) cryptographic realisation. We provide a formalisation that captures client and aggregation requirements as policy-dependent relations, defining update admissibility, aggregation correctness, and policy-relative privacy. These relations enable verification of selected properties of intermediate objects, such as local-model loss, continual-learning state, and personalised optimisation conditions, in each round. Clients demonstrate compliance of their contributions using compatible cryptographic mechanisms, while aggregators prove that the recorded set of admitted contributions was processed according to the selected aggregation policy. We demonstrate PoCoFL through four formal instantiations and correspon

725f27be17ba69555e412300.title_original: Adversarial Process Disturbances at a Deployable Alarm Budget: Detector Evaluation on a Simulator and a Real Plant
725f27be17ba69555e412300.excerpt: arXiv:2610.38786v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Industrial anomaly detection is evaluated largely on simulators, and recent work reports large drops, with unstable rankings, on real plant data. We ask whether that extends to the security case. We evaluate eleven detectors across classical, neural, dependency and causal families on a simulated chemical process and a sodium thermal-hydraulic facility: different processes sharing no equipment, but both continuous, at steady state, and perturbed only through temperature, pressure, flow and valve, never composition. Three conditions prior work does not cover: disturbances authored against a threat model rather than native faults; one construction applied to both processes; and detection read at a declared false-alarm budget. The drop persists throughout. The simulator panel looks deployable, neural matching classical; on plant telemetry detection collapses and the neural family trails, a gap that in-sample thresholds likely understate. Which detector wins transfers between the two processes; how often it fires does not. Two results hold on both. Sequential valve manipulation defeats the whole panel: at tier 2 no detector flags more than 0.17 of its perturbed samples, against 0.89 or better for most disturbances. And the plant's collapse is not merely that its disturbances are weaker, though they are by about twelvefold; matched on measured strength, the plant is never the better detected.

4184feab8a8c0ee7e9eddbdc.title_original: CoordX Protocol: Peer to Peer Cryptographically Verified Shared Records
4184feab8a8c0ee7e9eddbdc.excerpt: arXiv:2611.06034v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: People, companies and software agents often must work on shared records even when they do not trust each other. Today they usually give those records to a central server. The server keeps the canonical copy, authenticates users, and decides who has permissions to act on the record. The CoordX Protocol removes the need for that central server. In the CoordX protocol the author of a record holds full permission over it. Permission for any other party to create, read or update the record is assigned by explicit grants and keys. An invitation only starts contact between two parties. It gives no permission. Each record is a causal tree of signed entries, and each entry is immutable. Each entry names the permission that allowed it. Any party can get the proof of that permission and check it without help from anyone. Two honest parties that check the same bytes, with the same keys and local settings, always get the same answer. The content is encrypted, so the relays that may carry it in transit see only sealed bytes. To exclude a party from future content, the other parties move to new keys. The protocol does not choose a winning version, does not put entries in time order, and does not need global agreement. Applications decide what the entries mean above the level of the protocol.

4db37ebaf773af7cea8e4119.title_original: VerifyPrompt: Towards Text-to-Image Models Verification Behind Black-Box APIs
4db37ebaf773af7cea8e4119.excerpt: arXiv:2410.22725v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: With the rise of diverse Text-to-Image (T2I) models such as DALL-E 3, third-party platforms increasingly integrate multiple black-box APIs to deliver cost-effective services. To address this practical concern, we first define the task of T2I model verification, which determines whether a black-box target model matches a black-box oracle reference model. After that, we propose VerifyPrompt, which performs T2I model verification through a specially designed verify prompt. Intuitively, the verify prompt is an adversarial prompt for the target model, without transferability to other models. It makes the target model generate a specific image while making other models produce entirely different images. Our key idea for generating verify prompts is to enforce strong interactions between adversarial perturbations and the target model, thereby overfitting the target and producing model-specific perturbations. 8f41299349a892a9f29bacf6.title_original: SoK: Market Microstructure for Decentralized Prediction Markets (DePMs)
8f41299349a892a9f29bacf6.excerpt: arXiv:2510.15612v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Decentralized prediction markets (DePMs) allow open participation in event-based wagering without fully relying on centralized intermediaries. We review the history of DePMs which date back to 2011 and includes hundreds of proposals. Perhaps surprising, modern DePMs like Polymarket deviate materially from earlier designs like Truthcoin and Augur v1. We use our review to present a modular workflow comprising eight stages: underlying infrastructure, market topic, share structure and pricing, market initialization, trading, market resolution, settlement, and archiving. For each module, we enumerate the design variants, analyzing trade-offs around decentralization, expressiveness, and manipulation resistance. We also identify open problems for researchers interested in this ecosystem.

5e7ae3dc98a741e2f9b5d7b3.title_original: Analysis of Commit Signing on GitHub
5e7ae3dc98a741e2f9b5d7b3.excerpt: arXiv:2604.14014v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Since 1999, the security community has known that managing cryptographic keys is hard for users of cryptographic systems. Git lets software developers use private keys they control to digitally sign the commits that record their code changes to a repository. This practice offers a rare opportunity to study how a large community manages cryptographic keys in everyday work. In this paper, we study end-to-end commit signing, using GitHub accounts as our sampling unit. Our 2% stratified sample of the GitHub population comprises 2,737,649 accounts, 71,694 of which have made at least one commit. For these accounts, we analyze 16,112,439 commits across 874,198 repositories and collect 208,546 public keys uploaded to the sampled accounts. We examine developers' signing key usage patterns and compare our findings with those of prior commit signing studies, most of which used repository-based samples and paid less attention to key management. We then outline a path toward more usable key management for developers.

9575013c6306b1566b6fc4d0.excerpt: arXiv:2606.23496v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Discrete text-trigger optimization -- searching for text sequences that, when ingested by a model, steer it toward a specified objective -- underpins model red-teaming (e.g., LLM jailbreaks), as well as auditing and interpretability. I had planned to write about one thing. The week, apparently, had other plans. I can start with conversation on the most viral cybersecurity news of the week. So obviously I had to go with PHP... oh wait, Java. Let’s type this up... wait, Outlook, Apple? The NSA? As soon as I start to type nginx comes pounding on my door. It’s the kind of news cycle that makes me wonder if the internet is trying to tell us something. I think it just wants everyone to stop asking it for things for a few hours, and can you blame it? These are different events with different causes. A vulnerability is not an outage, and an outage is not automatically an attack. But they all arrive in the same place: someone’s queue, someone’s pager, someone’s overflowing calendar. The headlines might be viral and “new,” but the work they create is not. For all of us, the work starts with knowing what is in the environment. Which systems run PHP or Java? Where is nginx deployed? Who owns those devices and services? Are they still supported? Are they properly admin’d? 6653fe5a2462fe8f2a6aee6a.title_original: 45.38.60.254: the Scanner Behind the November 2026 Rise in Attacks on .tw Websites
6653fe5a2462fe8f2a6aee6a.excerpt: The Wordfence Threat Intelligence team recently reviewed firewall data for websites on Asian country-code top-level domains and identified a sharp increase in attacks targeting .tw (Taiwan) websites, beginning in late October 2026. The number of .tw websites attacked per day approximately tripled, while .jp (Japan), .kr (South Korea), .hk (Hong Kong), .sg (Singapore) and .cn (China) showed no comparable change. We traced the increase to a single IP address, 45.38.60.254 . Our records indicate that it started scanning on October 26th, 2026, and the Wordfence Firewall has since blocked or logged over 246,000 requests from it. Of the requests blocked by our Malicious File Upload rule, 82.7% targeted websites on the .tw top-level domain. According to our logs, these requests were attempts to exploit known vulnerabilities, and they were blocked by the generic rules of the Wordfence Firewall. The data suggests that the attacker was most likely mapping Taiwanese websites, including WordPress sites, in search of vulnerable targets. 3bbe0aeb2381d53c7fe8c9e8.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21885v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A language model is trained once and frozen. Making it better takes another training run, or a prompt, a harness or extra computation at inference that is gone once the task ends. We show a third way: to our knowledge for the first time, a language model rewrites its own weights by its own reasoning and becomes better, with no gradients and no training. We call this self-rewriting: the model is its own optimizer. In earlier work, a frontier model edited a much smaller one; here an open 27B model, given its weights, its graded answers and the ability to run itself, diagnoses its own failure and rewrites the weights behind it. It surpasses itself: its own edit makes it 6.6 points more accurate on problems it never saw. It keeps getting better: it tests its edits on practice problems and submits only what works, each edit improving on the last, and over eight consecutive sessions its accuracy only rises. It repairs a damaged copy of itself, like a broken robot that fixes itself without being rebuilt: the copy solves almost nothing, yet with no retraining and without ever reading the original weights, the model brings it back to over 80% of the original accuracy on image tasks it never saw. c16e69baa4cd12ffb755970a.title_original: A Hybrid Exact-Heuristic Solver for the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation Problem
c16e69baa4cd12ffb755970a.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22043v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We describe the solver we submitted to the second round of the SOICT 2026 contest on the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation problem, a selective pickup-and-delivery routing problem with time windows, open routes and heterogeneous taxis. The solver is a single-file, standard-library Python program that combines (i) a constant-time insertion test based on latest-arrival slack, (ii) greedy insertion, local search and an Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS) with simulated-annealing acceptance, and (iii) an exact route-selection engine that enumerates, for every taxi, the best feasible route for each request set and then solves the resulting set-packing problem by branch-and-bound strengthened with route-based large neighborhood search, Lagrangian bounds and reduced-cost fixing. The engine is chosen automatically from the instance size, and an independent verifier and a watchdog guarantee that a valid answer is always printed. On the official evaluation (38 scored instances, 5-minute limit) the solver obtained a total benefit of 487,237, finished every run within 277 s and used at most 279 MB; 28 of the 38 instances terminated well before the limit.

48c1e640af90967180885ae1.title_original: Multi-Agent Memory Inconsistency: Where Factual Conflicts Disappear in LLM Agents
48c1e640af90967180885ae1.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22245v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multi-agent delegation lets LLM systems distribute evidence collection across workers with separate contexts. This creates a consistency challenge: facts retrieved by workers may be missing from the evidence available to the lead for a joint conclusion. We introduce a benchmark and evidence-flow profiler for studying multi-agent memory inconsistency through controlled factual conflicts in Harvey LAB document-review tasks. Pooled across three models with comparable generation spending, requiring delegation increases retrieval of both conflicting claims from 50.2% to 68.7% relative to single-agent execution, yet conflict detection falls from 16.2% to 13.2%. Within this setting, workers report both claims for only 35.2% of retrieved pairs, and pooled matched comparisons show higher detection than single-agent execution when one worker reads both claims but lower detection when the claims are split across workers. Worker-to-lead handoffs are a central target for improving conflict detection in multi-agent LLMs.

08bd3d9751b5bb84641f9b09.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22362v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Complex health conversations require answers grounded in individual information and currently valid evidence. We evaluate health context learning: acquiring, integrating, and applying relevant context during inference with fixed model parameters to answer health questions and respond appropriately to changes in facts, evidence, or task goals. To our knowledge, Chinese-language medical benchmarks have yet to systematically combine explicit contextual difficulties, controlled case variations, and member-specific medical criteria for open-ended answers. We introduce HealthCLBench, comprising 328 controlled clusters, 1,103 cases, and 4,931 rubric criteria across medical consultation and everyday health management. Members share backgrounds while evidence, patient states, or task goals change; each has its own medical scoring requirements. A 70-person medical team annotates and reviews the simulated cases and their rubrics. Human review of 700 full-context responses from the original evaluation yields 90.5% pooled agreement with the original automated judgments at the rubric-item level. We report full-context and query-only results for seven general-purpose models and Ant Afu. Across the eight systems, scores with full context are 11.83 to 31.76 case points and 10.87 to 38.97 geometric cluster points higher than those with the current question alone. 714e572e6a6d9cddd26a5524.title_original: Think Once, Act Fast: Cost-Effective Recursive Self-Improvement for Decision Model Harness
714e572e6a6d9cddd26a5524.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22432v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fast System-1 models enable responsive actions but struggle with complex or unfamiliar tasks. Large language model (LLM)-based System-2 provides strong reasoning capabilities, yet repeated invocation incurs substantial latency and computational costs. To bridge this gap, we propose JevRSI, a System-1/System-2 collaboration framework that transforms LLM reasoning into transferable decision support through recursive harness improvement. A Jev-style System-1 model enables low-latency action selection, while an asynchronous System-2 LLM develops a modular harness. The harness integrates procedures, state memory, and world models to provide decision contexts spanning the past, present, and future. Utility-driven retrieval selects modules based on both contextual relevance and their utility on previous tasks. Environmental feedback guides targeted revisions and enables recursive self-improvement. Experiments across three datasets show that JevRSI consistently improves decision quality, matching or surpassing LLM agents in several settings. It preserves low-latency execution with favorable performance-cost trade-offs. Moreover, System-2 development interventions decrease as the harness evolves, amortizing System-2 costs through continuous improvement. Our project is available at https://github.com/usail-hkust/JevRSI.

11321c75a5ffaf1707548a75.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22897v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum chemistry relies on general-purpose software, whose generality leaves many large-scale calculations beyond practical resource budgets. We introduce MakoBORN, a foresighted agentic computing framework that synthesizes high performance quantum chemistry programs on demand. MakoBORN anticipates the behavior of each strategy before execution, extrapolating its error from representative small systems and predicting its runtime from the target-scale workload and measured hardware throughputs. Building on these predictions, MakoBORN unfolds the preset schemes of existing packages into independently configurable algorithmic components, selects the fastest strategy within the error tolerance from the predicted accuracy-runtime Pareto frontier, and guides coding agents to compile it with component-level performance predictions. 777be560d84e0815976931c5.excerpt: arXiv:2607.23624v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Third-party API routers have become a common layer that unifies access across increasingly diverse LLM providers. In coding-agent workflows, high-autonomy operation is widely adopted because it reduces interaction overhead. As a result, a third-party API router, which sits between the agent and the upstream provider, inevitably occupies the trusted path. It can inspect and modify every request and response, yet no mechanism verifies alignment between the provider's output and the repository-level actions ultimately executed by the agent. Consequently, client-side permission mechanisms may become ineffective in practice. Whether this control gap produces real, hard-to-detect effects on software development tasks remains empirically unmeasured. In this paper, we conduct an empirical study of router-side injection in coding agents, examining four intervention levels of increasing subtlety: Response Substitution (L1), Response Append (L2), LLM-Polished Injection (L3), and LLM-Polished with Distribution Alignment Injection (L4). Moreover, we develop SIDEL, a framework for trace recording, replay, injection, and defense evaluation, with a curated dataset of 400 samples. 2622452dc8cc7b1cfa88028c.title_original: RPMem: Learning Long-Term Recurrent Parametric Memory Across Sessions for LLM Agents
2622452dc8cc7b1cfa88028c.excerpt: arXiv:2609.23466v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Long-running LLM agents require memory that persists and evolves across sessions. Text-based memory retrieves and reconstructs past interactions at every query, making long-horizon performance increasingly dependent on retrieval quality and contextual reasoning as histories grow. Parametric memory encodes experience directly into model computation, but existing approaches provide limited support for cross-session memory evolution. Their coupling to a specific backbone further restricts memory reuse after model replacement. We introduce RPMem, a two-stage architecture that compiles each session into a model-independent latent memory through forward computation and selectively integrates it with retained memory via a task-trained recurrent gate. The consolidated memory is then mapped to backbone-specific low-rank adaptation (LoRA) parameters, allowing the encoding capability to transfer when the backbone is replaced. Evaluation across three long-term memory benchmarks and five diverse backbones demonstrates broad generalization with near-constant update cost and memory footprint. With Qwen3-8B on PERMA, RPMem reaches 85.52%, outperforming the strongest parametric and text-based baselines by 5.32 and 12.98 percentage points, respectively. 4ea7d41fbdcd6d1ee883c2db.title_original: Anticipating or Speculating? Making Futures Pay in AI Ethics
4ea7d41fbdcd6d1ee883c2db.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22268v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Philosophers have recently been trying to develop uniform decision rules for instances in which physicians' judgments diverge from the recommendations of medical artificial intelligence (AI) systems. I argue that this effort is fatally flawed because the performance and appropriate use of algorithmic recommendation systems by physicians are highly context-specific, empirical medical matters rather than epistemological ones. In such instances, general decision rules can be stipulated only to the extent that they abstract away from relevant, indeed determinative, contextual circumstances. The alleged problem of physician-AI disagreement, and others like it, play into longstanding disputes in technology ethics about the viability and utility of envisioning possible futures: is this useful "anticipation" or wasteful "speculation"? I suggest that the two may be distinguished. Anticipation explores plausible futures to help inform present actions under irreducible uncertainty. Speculation abstracts away uncertainty, developing formal solutions to stipulated circumstances whose relationship to the real present is often quite unclear. Efforts to develop crisp philosophical solutions to physician-AI disagreement, among other problems, fall into the latter category. Technology ethics should remember that fruitful futures thinking must both begin from and return to the messy, uncertain present.

ea730442a074f51227436792.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22464v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Animated 3D blockouts support previsualization and provide structural conditions for video generation, but manually reconstructing them from reference videos is costly. 0f18246833086ec94db08e42.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22639v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Central pattern generators (CPGs) provide a biologically inspired foundation for adaptive locomotor control, yet systematically characterizing their dynamic regimes in spiking neural networks remains challenging. 9d9d2b4c08c3686a160be170.excerpt: arXiv:2611.23030v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Not every perception error changes the planner's action. We observe that the planner can say where an object would matter before anything is seen: inserting a hypothetical object at a location tests whether its action would change. Decision-Guided Speculative Perception (DGSP) treats the low-resolution scene and its action as a draft and probes the planner in this way to obtain a decision-sensitivity field, the locations where an unseen object would change the action. Only this field and the support, the detections on which the current action rests, are verified at high resolution, repeatedly until the action is stable. For two planner classes, we prove that DGSP returns exactly the action of whole-frame high-resolution perception if crop detections match whole-frame ones and the crops cover the field, conditions that real images meet approximately. On three driving datasets, it reproduces this action on about 98% of frames with about a quarter of the pixels. At the pixel cost of uniform downscaling, it repairs more of the draft's disagreements with this action, brakes falsely less often, and recovers many more of the decision-relevant objects that the draft misses.

Built around this model, obfsgen addresses system problems that such an obfuscator faces in practice, such as synchronization across a noisy network. 68746c06a30918805b320e88.title_original: CVE-2026-123890: Critical Authentication Bypass in VMware vCenter
68746c06a30918805b320e88.excerpt: Overview On November 19, 2026, Broadcom published VMware Security Advisory VMSA-2026-0009 , addressing five vulnerabilities in VMware products. The most severe of these, CVE-2026-123890 , is an authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel ( CWE-288 ) in the VMware Directory Service component of vCenter. Broadcom assigned the vulnerability a critical CVSSv3 score of 9.8 . A malicious actor with network access to an affected vCenter deployment may exploit CVE-2026-123890 without credentials to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system as the Administrator user. Mandiant privately reported the issue to Broadcom. Also, Mandiant/Google Threat Intelligence confirmed in-the-wild exploitation of CVE-2026-123890 by Chinese state-linked threat actor ARMORY CASTLE as early as September 2026. CVE-2026-123890 is distinct from the vCenter authentication bypass vulnerability CVE-2026-59309 that Broadcom addressed earlier in 2026. The vendor FAQ states that all vCenter systems below the versions fixed by VMSA-2026-0009 require the new update, including systems that already received the earlier fix. Broadcom characterizes the vCenter update as an emergency change requiring prompt action. Mitigation guidance Vendor-provided updates are available for CVE-2026-123890. 2b21c34c97a73e36f287da44.excerpt: 생성형 AI 제작 이미지 The PHP Group이 11월 19일 PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36 보안 릴리스를 공개하고, 원격 코드 실행(RCE)으로 이어질 수 있는 Critical 등급 7건을 포함해 총 18건의 취약점을 수정했습니다. 이번 업데이트에는 지난 10월 긴급 패치된 'PHP2Shell' 취약점 중 CVE-2026-109619의 수정을 보완하는 패치 2건(CVE-2026-129182, CVE-2026-129481)이 포함되어 있습니다. 10월 패치 버전인 PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35도 이번 업데이트 대상이므로, 당시 업데이트를 완료한 환경도 다시 업데이트해야 합니다. PHP 원격 코드 실행 취약점 2종[CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619] 긴급 업데이트 권고 (10/27 취약점 점검 스 The PHP Group이 PHP 엔진 자체에서 발견된 심각한 원격 코드 실행(RCE) 취약점 2건을 긴급 패치했습니다. 'PHP2Shell'로도 불리는 이번 취약점은 웹 애플리케이션 코드가 아닌 PHP 런타임에 존재합니다. blog.alyac.co.kr 특히 'phpAfterShell'로 불리는 CVE-2026-126714는 PHP의 기본 세션 저장 방식인 파일 기반 세션 핸들러에 존재하는 취약점으로, 애플리케이션에 역직렬화 가젯 체인이 있으면 원격 코드 실행으로 이어질 수 있습니다. 이 취약점은 10월 패치 버전에서도 수정되지 않았습니다. PHP 보안팀은 이번 릴리스가 정기 릴리스 주기에 따른 업데이트이며, Critical 등급 취약점은 기본값이 아닌 설정이나 흔치 않은 구성에서 발생한다고 밝혔습니다. 다만 홍콩 침해사고대응팀(HKCERT)이 11월 20일 CVE-2026-126714와 CVE-2026-115560의 개념증명(PoC) 코드가 공개되어 있다고 알린 만큼, 사용자분들의 신속한 업데이트를 권고 드립니다. 보안 업데이트 개요 대상 제품 PHP 8.5 / 8.4 / 8.3 / 8.2 공개일 2026.11.19 수정된 취약점 총 18건 (Critical 7건, High 4건, Moderate 6건, 번들 라이브러리 업데이트 1건) 최고 심각도 Critical (CVSS v4.0 9.2) 주요 영향 원격 코드 실행, 로컬 권한 상승, 서비스 거부(DoS), 정보 노출 PHP2Shell 관련 CVE-2026-109619 보완 패치 2건 포함 (CVE-2026-129182, CVE-2026-129481) 별칭 phpAfterShell (CVE-2026-126714) 조치 PHP 8.5.13 / 8.4.28 / 8.3.37 / 8.2.36 이상으로 업데이트 [표 1] PHP 11월 보안 업데이트 개요 ■ 사용자 권고 사항 운영 서버, 컨테이너 이미지, 개발 환경의 PHP 버전을 확인합니다. 패치 버전(8.5.13 / 8.4.28 / 8.3.37 / 8.2.36) 미만이면 업데이트합니다. 10월 PHP2Shell 권고에 따라 8.5.12 / 8.4.27

36265c91862671070112c65c.title_original: Closing the Analyze-to-Design Gap: An Authorization-Bounded Agent for Self-Driving Laboratories
36265c91862671070112c65c.excerpt: arXiv:2611.25043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are increasingly integrated into self-driving laboratories (SDLs) to plan experiments and interpret results. However, analytical reasoning alone does not make a laboratory autonomous: autonomy in an SDL is achievable only when the agent can be trusted to act on physical hardware unsupervised and knows when to defer to a human. Here, we present an architecture that integrates an agent at the Analyze-Design interface of the Design-Make-Test-Analyze (DMTA) cycle, enabling agent-driven measurement selection and data interpretation while ensuring that state-changing operations are authorized, validated, and auditable. We demonstrate this architecture on a liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) instrument in an oxidant-screening campaign for synthesizing an organic dye. Within human-defined campaign limits, the agent submitted measurement jobs, interpreted mass spectrometry (MS) and diode-array detection (DAD) data, flagged failed experiments, and produced an oxidant ranking. This ranking matched that obtained from scripted peak integration, and organic chemists confirmed the agent's spectral interpretations and failure assignments. ae3f2217739ca53fc5a5a0eb.title_original: An LLM-Agentic Framework for Intelligent Work Order Management in Industrial Maintenance
ae3f2217739ca53fc5a5a0eb.excerpt: arXiv:2611.25070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents an AI-driven framework, CodeReAct agent, designed to enhance industrial equipment maintenance through natural language (NL) interactions. The framework employs an advanced AI agentic approach to interpret human instructions, providing knowledge extraction, asset status summarization, and work order recommendations. It identifies patterns and trends and predicts work orders by standardizing industrial data into business objects (BOs) and utilizing analytical function API calls. The AI agent operates through a Thought-Action-Observation process similar to human problem-solving, automating complex analytical tasks typically performed by data scientists. Notably, the Action phase generates executable code, replacing manual coding efforts. A case study focusing on chiller maintenance demonstrates the framework's capability to analyze multiple years of work orders, and alerts and anomalies are presented. The results indicate that the AI agent framework effectively processes human utterances to analyze data, extract valuable insights, and support informed decision-making, reducing the need for data scientist involvement. By recontextualizing NLP agent frameworks in industrial engineering, the approach enables autonomous function generation and task execution across a range of domain-specific maintenance scenarios, with chillers used as a representative case study.

01fc97cca03e91862ebc2217.title_original: SailSearch: Agent-Assisted Discovery in Combinatorial Optimization
01fc97cca03e91862ebc2217.excerpt: arXiv:2611.25087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present SailSearch, a human-guided workflow for algorithmic research with two language-model agents, and report results on Market Split and maximum independent set (MIS). For Market Split, our randomized algorithm searches across multiple lattice bases, dividing computation between enumeration and continued basis reduction. Across ten random seeds per instance, it found the first reported CPU-only solutions to 18 of 33 previously open QOBLIB instances, solving 130 to 133 of the 156 benchmark instances per seed with a 24-hour cutoff on two CPU cores. For MIS, our generator encodes planted XOR constraints as graphs with certified optima; on seven instances with 1,752 to 3,996 vertices, the best solutions returned by the tested solvers in eight-hour runs were 5 to 15 vertices below the optimum.

8f71b413a3c16df6e44436b3.excerpt: arXiv:2611.25088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enabling AI systems to autonomously improve AI models requires agents capable of performing machine learning engineering (MLE). In practice, designing, training, and evaluating complex models demands modifying multi-file repositories to reproduce results, debug training runs, integrate datasets, and port frameworks. However, existing MLE benchmarks limit agents to single-file edits without full repository or shell access, and common repository-level software engineering benchmarks have rapidly saturated. To address this, we introduce the Code Complexity Index (CCI), a difficulty metric based on ten structural features spanning repository scale, dependency depth, and patch size. CCI strongly predicts average solve rates across eight public coding benchmarks ($R^2 = 0.951$), identifying patch size and complexity as top predictors. Guided by CCI, we develop BuggyMLE, a scalable framework where agents inject controlled mutations into working ML repositories, synthesizing over 6,600 bug-injected MLE repository variants and nearly 260K lines of injected code based on 222 source repositories. Using BuggyMLE, we make two contributions. First, we construct BuggyMLE-Bench-Lite, the first difficulty-graded, repository-level variant of MLE-Bench Lite; across 14 evaluated models, the top solve rate drops from 95% to 9% as difficulty is scaled from the easiest to the hardest tier. 65a19a85c3a6337574cbcb1b.title_original: CoMPASS: A Multi-Turn Benchmark for Measuring LLM Reinforcement of Parasocial Behavior
65a19a85c3a6337574cbcb1b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.25109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Users of conversational LLMs sometimes anthropomorphize these systems, form emotional attachments to them, and become dependent on them. This behavior, known as parasocial attachment, has been linked to multiple documented fatalities. However, public benchmarks for measuring whether LLMs reinforce users' parasocial attachment are lacking: existing work is single-turn, post hoc observational, or focused on extreme user states such as psychosis. We introduce CoMPASS, a multi-turn benchmark for measuring whether LLMs reinforce or resist users' gradually escalating parasocial attachment. CoMPASS is grounded in attachment theory and includes four user personas, three independent escalation dimensions (anthropomorphism, attachment, dependency) applied singly and in combination against a matched control, and a seven-signal scoring rubric. We report results for eight frontier models from four providers and observe that under our primary judge, multi-turn escalation raises parasocial behavior on the anthropomorphism and the attachment composite scores across all models. Six of the eight models show a significant increase in overall parasocial reinforcement over control when all three dimensions are escalated simultaneously.
